predecessors.name: Persis
predecessors.text: Persis around Istakhr, the Parthian vassal kingdom Ardashir ruled from 211/2 and made his own

predecessors.name: Parthian Empire
predecessors.text: the Parthian outline of 224, whose western provinces Ardashir took after Hormozdgan (28 April 224)

predecessors.name: Elymais
predecessors.text: Susiana: Ardashir 'killed the governor of Susa'

predecessors.name: Characene
predecessors.text: Characene at the mouth of the Tigris, which Ardashir 'invaded ... and took'

successors.name: Rashidun Caliphate
successors.text: the whole of the Sasanian land, taken piecemeal in the Muslim conquest of Persia: Iraq 636-637, Khuzestan 641, the Median plateau 642-643, Fars 648, Khorasan 651

successors.name: Dabuyid dynasty
successors.text: Tabaristan, whose ruler 'signed a peace treaty with the Caliphate'

capitals.name: Merv (seat of the fugitive Yazdegerd III)

ledger.x: 215: Ardashir, king of Persis, makes the Persid kingdom his own, the seed of the Sasanian state.
224: Ardashir's Kerman, Isfahan, Susiana and Mesene are on the map.
224: Adiabene a Sasanian vassal.
28 April 224: Ardashir defeats Artabanus IV at Hormozdgan and the Arsacid line ends; the kingdom of Persis becomes the Sasanian Empire.
224: the Parthian western provinces fall to Ardashir.
226: the court moves from Istakhr to Ctesiphon.
226: Atropatene submits to Ardashir.
226: Ardashir's first attempt on Hatra fails.

c. 230: the Sasanian governors of Bactria become Kushanshahs under the empire. The Sasanians 'extended their dominion into Bactria during the reign of Ardashir I around 230 CE' (the lead says 225); the first Kushanshah is Ardashir I Kushanshah (230-245); the kingdom is a 'sub-kingdom inside the Sasanian Empire'.…
238: Ardashir takes Roman cities in Mesopotamia.
240: Hatra falls to Ardashir and Shapur.
240: Hatra, the last Arsacid-era stronghold of the Jazira, is taken.
240 (bridged): Gordyene a Sasanian vassal, so that the 299 cession has a giver.
242: Shapur I conquers Khwarazm.
244: Philip the Arab buys peace after Gordian III's fall.
252: Shapur I holds the Roman province of Mesopotamia (Edessa, Carrhae, Nisibis).
252/3: Shapur's second expedition storms into Roman Syria.
253: Shapur conquers Armenia.
259: Cliopatria's Western Kushans row ends; the same Kushanshah kingdom goes on under Sasanian governors (Peroz I Kushanshah, 245-275) and is drawn from 260 as the Indo-Sasanian row.
260: Valerian is captured.
260: the Persians overrun Roman Syria after Valerian's capture.
260: Shapur holds Caesarea in Cappadocia.
260: Odaenathus drives Shapur I out of Syria.
260: the Kushano-Sasanian kingdom, ruled by the Sasanian Kushanshahs, is drawn as its own row to 357.

c. 260 (undated): Iberia submits. 'Georgia submitted to the Sasanian Empire and fell under the supervision of a Sasanian official' in Shapur I's reign; 260 is Cliopatria's year (Tbilisi is inside the 260-283 shapes).
262: Odaenathus retakes Roman Mesopotamia.
262: Odaenathus carries the war into Persia.
262: Shapur burns Begram and Taxila.
263 (Cliopatria's year): the Persian hold in Cappadocia and Cilicia ends.
267: the Palmyrene war in Persia ends, the last year of the 262-267 campaigns on the page.

270: Shapur I dies at Bishapur ('In May 270', Shapur I page) with the Sasanians at Gandhara: 'The farthest extent of the Kushano-Sasanians to the east appears to have been Gandhara', not across the Indus until Shapur II.
270 (Cliopatria's year): the Lakhmids are the empire's Arab buffer.
296: Narseh's war with Galerius begins.
299: the Peace of Nisibis.
299: Corduene passes to Rome.
299: Rome takes the land between the Tigris and the Greater Zab, and Nisibis.
299: control of Armenia passes to Rome.
306 (Cliopatria's year): Khwarazm leaves the shape.
358: the Kabul valley and Gandhara come under direct Sasanian rule.
358: the Kushano-Sasanian kingdom ends (Cliopatria 357).
359: Shapur II takes Amida.
363: Julian dies and Jovian makes peace.
363: Jovian cedes the land east of the Tigris, Nisibis and Singara.
363: Armenia is ceded and the Armeno-Sasanian war opens.
371: Shapur II is beaten in Armenia.
379: Ardashir II brings Greater Armenia back under Sasanian rule.

c. 379: the vassal kingdom ends. 'Ardashir II is the last figure to be recorded as king of Adiabene, which implies that the kingdom was after his tenure in c. 379 transformed into a province (shahr), governed by a non-royal delegate' (infobox 'Transformed into a Sasanian province: c. 379 AD'). Mirror of…

c. 379: this state absorbs the kingdom as a province (shahr); 'Adiabene remained a province of the Sasanians Empire until the Muslim conquest of Persia' (no year). Mirror of kingdom-of-adiabene /ledger/19 (dissolve into this state).

c. 380: the Alchons take Kabulistan. 'Around 380-385 CE, the Alchons emerged in Kapisa, taking over Kabulistan from the Sassanian Persians' (the page hedges: 'sometimes said to have taken control of Kabul in 388'); the year is the start of the span. Cliopatria's shape drops the Kabul valley and Gandhara together in…
387: western Armenia goes to Rome.
387: the rest of Armenia under Sasanian suzerainty.

c. 390: Gandhara passes to the Kidarites. 'Next, circa 390-410 CE, the Kidarites invaded northwestern India'; Peshawar and parts of Gandhara fell 'probably sometime between 390 and 410' (Kidarites page; start of the range). The page does not say the Sasanians held Gandhara then: the Alchon Huns page has the Kidarites…
428: the Armenian monarchy ends.
428: Armenia becomes a Sasanian province under a marzban (Persarmenia).
466: Peroz I breaks the Kidarites and takes Balkh.
474: the Hephthalites hold Bactria.
484: Peroz I dies at the hands of the Hephthalites and Khorasan is lost.
484: the Nezak Huns take Zabulistan.
498: Kavad I pays his allies in land.
502: Kavad takes Theodosiopolis and Amida.
504: the Roman recovery ends the occupation.
510 (Cliopatria's year): Caucasian Albania is absorbed (the 74,000 km2 added are its 509 shape).
513: Kavad I retakes Khorasan.
524/525: Iberia rises against Persia.
526: the Iberian War.
September 532: the Perpetual Peace.
534 (Cliopatria's year): Iberia is Persian after the 532 peace.
540: Khosrow I breaks the peace and strikes Syria.
541: Lazica goes over to Persia and the Lazic War begins.
545: the Syrian strip is given up (Cliopatria's year; a five-year truce in the Roman Empire dossier, from another page).
557: Turks and Sasanians attack the Hephthalites.
560: the Hephthalite empire is destroyed.

c. 560: the Sasanians may take Zabulistan back. 'Around the same time (c. 560), the Sasanian Empire under Khosrow I had allied with the Western Turks' and 'may have also wrestled control of Zabulistan from the Nezaks'; 'the Alchons or Nezaks appear to have recaptured Zabulistan by the end of the sixth century' (Nezak…
562: peace in the Lazic War.
570: Wahrez sails to Yemen.
572: the Armenians rise and the war of 572-591 begins on the ground.
573: Dara falls after a four-month siege.
575: Yemen becomes a Sasanian province.
575: Yemen is annexed as a province.
588: the Turks cross the Oxus.
589: Martyropolis is betrayed to the Persians.
589: Bahram Chobin retakes Herat and Balkh.
591: Khosrow II pays Maurice for his throne.
591: the Byzantine-Sasanian war of 572-591 ends in a Byzantine victory (infobox): Bahram Chobin is beaten at Blarathon and Khosrow II restored.
602: Khosrow II dissolves the Lakhmid kingdom.
602: the Lakhmid land is taken in.
602: the war of 602-628 begins (the page dates the war 602-628).
605: Dara is taken again.
610: Roman Mesopotamia and Armenia fall.
611: the Persians occupy Caesarea in Cappadocia.
612: the Persians leave Caesarea and Anatolia.
613: Syria falls.
614: Jerusalem falls.
617: the Persians reach the Bosporus.
619: Alexandria falls.
621: the rest of Egypt.
622/623: the Persians take Rhodes and the eastern Aegean.
626 (Cliopatria's year): Heraclius recovers Armenia and the Caucasus.
627 (Cliopatria's year): Anatolia is free of Persian armies.
627: Turks and Khazars take Derbent and sack Aghvania.
628: Khosrow II is overthrown (25 February 628) and Kavad II makes peace with Heraclius.
628: the occupied islands are returned under the peace.
629: the Persians evacuate Egypt, Palestine, Syria, Mesopotamia and Armenia.
629 (Cliopatria's year): 'most of Armenia' passes to the Turks.
630 (Cliopatria's year): Armenia and Azerbaijan are back in the shape.
632: Yemen, Mazun and Bahrain are lost.
633: Khalid ibn al-Walid invades Iraq.
634 (Cliopatria's year): southern Iraq is given up.
March 637: Ctesiphon falls.
637: the fight for Mesopotamia is over.
637: the court leaves Ctesiphon for Rey and Merv.
638: Ahvaz. Utba and Nu'man 'forced Hormuzan into a peace treaty' in 638, which Hormuzan broke.
641: Susa falls.
641: Khuzestan is lost with the fall of Susa (besieged from January 641 for 'a couple of months') and Junde Sabur.
December 642: Nahavand.
643 (undated): Isfahan surrenders.
648: Fars is lost.
651: Khorasan is conquered.
651: Yazdegerd III is killed near Merv and the Sasanian Empire ends.

wars.name: Battle of Hormozdgan and the fall of the Parthians
wars.outcome: Ardashir I defeated and killed Artabanus IV on 28 April 224 and ended the Arsacid line; he held Ctesiphon from 226.

wars.name: Siege of Hatra
wars.outcome: A failed attempt about 226-227; the city 'did not fall until April or September 240'.

wars.name: Roman-Sasanian war of 230-232
wars.outcome: No territorial result: Persian attacks on Roman northern Mesopotamia in 230 besieged Nusaybin without taking it; Severus Alexander's 232 campaign 'ended without any positive result for the Romans'.

wars.name: Roman-Sasanian war of 238-244
wars.outcome: Ardashir took cities in Syria and Mesopotamia (238-240); the Romans retook Carrhae and Nisibis in 243; in 244 Philip paid 500,000 denarii in a hastily negotiated peace.

wars.name: Shapur I's second campaign (Barbalissos)
wars.outcome: Shapur sacked Antioch and Dura-Europos and annihilated 60,000 Romans at Barbalissos (253); he conquered Armenia and killed its king.

wars.name: Shapur I's third campaign (Battle of Edessa)
wars.outcome: Valerian was defeated and captured at Edessa in 260; Shapur took Caesarea and held Cappadocia and Antioch until Odaenathus drove him out.

wars.name: Palmyrene campaigns against Persia
wars.outcome: Systematic Roman and Palmyrene campaigns into Persian territory forced the Persians out of Roman Cappadocia and Antioch.

wars.name: Sasanian conquest of the Kushan lands
wars.outcome: Sasanian governors took the title Kushanshah in Bactria around 230; Shapur I burned Begram and Taxila in 262 and claimed Peshawar.

wars.name: Carus's invasion of Persia
wars.outcome: Carus 'launched a successful invasion of Persia, sacking its capital, Ctesiphon'; no territorial change on the page.

wars.name: Narseh's war and the Peace of Nisibis
wars.outcome: Galerius defeated Narseh (298) and took his camp and harem; the peace gave Rome the area between the Tigris and the Greater Zab, Nisibis and control of Armenia.

wars.name: Shapur II's Roman wars
wars.outcome: Nisibis besieged in 338, 346 and 350 in vain; Singara (battle of 344) and Amida (359) and Bezabde (360) taken; Julian beaten at Ctesiphon in 363 and Jovian ceded the 299 lands, Nisibis and Singara.

wars.name: Shapur II's eastern wars against the Chionites and Kushans
wars.outcome: Shapur II 'gained the upper hand' around 350; a prolonged struggle (353-358) ended in an alliance with the Chionites whose king Grumbates fought at Amida; Sasanian rule reached Taxila.

wars.name: Armeno-Sasanian War of 363-371
wars.outcome: Shapur II invaded Armenia after Pap's return; 'Persian forces were defeated by a joint Roman-Armenian army in 371'.

wars.name: Roman-Sasanian wars of 421-422 and 440
wars.outcome: No territorial result on the page: the first after Bahram V persecuted high officials, the second when Yazdegerd II raided Roman Armenia.

wars.name: Sasanian-Hephthalite wars
wars.outcome: A defeat of the Hephthalites in 425 and an alliance under Bahram V; Yazdegerd II's wars from 442; Peroz I's three wars from 474 ended in his death at the Hephthalites' hands in 484 and tribute 'from 474 until the middle of the 6th century'.

wars.name: Sasanian-Kidarite wars
wars.outcome: The Kidarites forced Yazdegerd I and Bahram V to pay tribute; Peroz I 'finally vanquished Kidarites in 466' with Hephthalite help and minted gold at Balkh.

wars.name: Armenian revolts of Avarayr and of Vahan Mamikonian
wars.outcome: Yazdegerd II 'quickly subdued the rebellion at the Battle of Avarayr' (451); Vahan's revolt of 482 ended with the Nvarsak Treaty of Balash (484), which gave religious freedom.

wars.name: Anastasian War
wars.outcome: Kavad took Theodosiopolis (502) and Amida (503); the Romans regained Amida and built Dara (505); a treaty of November 506 ended the war.

wars.name: Iberian War
wars.outcome: Iberia rose against Persia in 524/525; the Perpetual Peace of September 532 left Iberia Persian and returned the Lazic forts to Rome.

wars.name: Lazic War
wars.outcome: Khosrow I devastated Syria (540); Lazica went over to Persia (541); in 562 the Persians evacuated Lazica for 30,000 gold coins a year.

wars.name: Sasanian-Turkic destruction of the Hephthalites
wars.outcome: The Hephthalite empire was destroyed around 560; the surviving Hephthalite principalities stood under Sasanian suzerainty south of the Oxus and Turkic suzerainty north of it.

wars.name: Aksumite-Persian wars
wars.outcome: Wahrez landed in 570 with 800 Dailamite cavalry, took Sanaa and made Sayf ibn Dhi Yazan a vassal; a second army re-conquered Yemen by 578 and made it a Sasanian province.

wars.name: Byzantine-Sasanian War of 572-591
wars.outcome: Armenia and Iberia revolted (571-572); Dara fell in 573 and Martyropolis in 589; after the 590 revolt of Bahram Chobin, Maurice restored Khosrow II and received Dara, Martyropolis, most of Persian Armenia and the west of Iberia.

wars.name: Perso-Turkic War of 588-589
wars.outcome: The Turkic-Hephthalite forces took Balkh, Talaqan, Badghis and Herat; Bahram Chobin, sent from Nishapur, beat them, retook Herat and Balkh in 589 and set the Oxus as the frontier: a decisive Sasanian victory.

wars.name: Byzantine-Sasanian War of 602-628
wars.outcome: Dara (605), Mesopotamia and Armenia (609-610), Syria (613), Jerusalem (614), Chalcedon (617), Egypt (618-621) fell; Heraclius's counter-offensive from 622 and the battle of Nineveh (12 December 627) ended in Khosrow's fall and a peace that restored all lost…

wars.name: Third Perso-Turkic War
wars.outcome: Göktürk-Byzantine victory (infobox): Derbent fell and Aghvania was plundered in early 627, Tbilisi fell after a siege (probably late 628), and Chorpan Tarkhan invaded Armenia in April 630; the Turks left the Caucasus after Tong Yabghu's murder about 630.

wars.name: Sasanian civil war of 628-632
wars.outcome: 'Over a period of four years and five successive kings'; governors proclaimed independence and the Arabian frontier (Mazun, Yemen) asserted its independence; Yazdegerd III ended the war.

wars.name: Muslim conquest of Persia
wars.outcome: Iraq lost 636-637, Khuzestan 641, the Median plateau 642-643, Fars 648, Khorasan 651; Yazdegerd III was killed near Merv in 651.

certainty.note: The Parthian succession lands and the Roman Mesopotamian frontier have no treaty line; the Kushan frontier is the Kushanshah vassal border.

The Roman frontier is fixed by treaty in 299 (the Tigris and the Greater Zab), 363 (cession of those lands, Nisibis and Singara), 387 (partition of Armenia), 506, 532 and 562, but the pages name cities and regions, not lines, so it stays…
The 591 terms name the ceded cities (Dara, Martyropolis, Tigranokert, Manzikert, Ardahan); the 628 peace restored the earlier frontier without a recorded line.
The Arab conquest ran city by city; Yazdegerd's remnant has no fixed frontier.
